## Free when you do it yourself. Paid when Trifold is the third party. {#the-rule}

<span class="kicker">Business model</span>

<div class="cards cards--2">
<div class="card card--green"><strong>Never paywalled</strong>
<ul>
<li>Verifying receipts and seals, for anyone</li>
<li>Data export: the business owns its books</li>
<li>Erasure and privacy tools</li>
<li>Correctness and security fixes</li>
<li>The receipt and seal specs (Apache-2.0)</li>
</ul></div>
<div class="card"><strong>What paid plans will sell</strong>
<ul>
<li>Automation and scheduling</li>
<li>Teams and collaboration</li>
<li>AI: Rifo <span class="tag tag--next">Next</span></li>
<li>Views across many schools</li>
<li>Trifold as witness <span class="tag tag--next">Next</span></li>
</ul></div>
</div>

<p class="fine">A self-hosted copy cannot produce Trifold's witness signature, so the premium tier will protect itself without a strict license.</p>

::: {.notes}
Sources: `docs/business/pricing-strategy.md` §1 ("The rule": anything a school can do on its own is free to self-host; anything that needs Trifold as the trusted third party is paid; the five things paid tiers sell; why the premium tier protects itself) and §2 ("Never paywall"). Same rule in `docs/business/business-plan.md` §5.

Correction applied (pricing-strategy §2 item 5, audited 2026-11-07): only the receipt and seal specs are open (Apache-2.0). The KPI spec and the event envelope schema are FSL today, so they are not called part of the open standard. Hosted plans are not built, so "will sell".
:::
